html:
SMTO-FIL-0057 — SMTO can't move these files directly to another drive

GUID: 635748fc-d9c9-4dbc-8011-05b6f4034d71
Slug: file-cross-device
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: fil

What happened

  • Files can't be moved between two different drives in one step, and SMTO couldn't switch to its safe copy-then-delete method for this request, so it stopped.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to list both the original folder and the destination folder. This shows whether anything was already moved before SMTO stopped.
  2. Ask SMTO to copy (not move) the files to the other drive. Copying works between drives and keeps the originals in place until you're sure.
  3. After you've checked the copies are complete, ask SMTO to delete the originals if you no longer need them. Deleting as a separate step means you can't lose files if the copy goes wrong.

What success looks like

  • The files are on the new drive, and the originals were removed only after you confirmed the copies.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the originals until you've confirmed the copies.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A rename or move failed with EXDEV (or Windows ERROR_NOT_SAME_DEVICE) because source and destination are on different filesystems and the automatic copy-then-delete fallback did not apply.

What this means

  • The OS returned EXDEV or Windows not-same-device status for an operation requiring same-filesystem rename behavior. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • The OS returned EXDEV or Windows not-same-device status for an operation requiring same-filesystem rename behavior.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect source/destination filesystem identities and the intended rename/copy semantics.

How to fix it

  • Check changed_paths and path_context in the result to see whether any change preceded the EXDEV failure (the fallback only runs when nothing has changed yet). Copy to the other filesystem with the file copy operation, verify the destination, then delete the source as a separate authorized step; never treat this as an atomic rename.
  • Use a supported copy/transfer workflow and verify the destination before explicitly removing the source when authorized. Do not treat a cross-volume copy as an atomic rename.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A supported explicit transfer is verified before any separately authorized source removal.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass the unsupported-feature check or reinterpret an unsupported response as success.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
